scope: The spectral theorem, a reciprocal-square-root estimate and a matrix-product bound control the change of coefficients.
Symmetric orthogonalization with the inverse square root of a positive overlap near the identity gives an exactly orthonormal orbital frame.

The full overlap matrix determines the transformation. For spectral overlap error δ at most one half, the one- and two-electron integral perturbations cost at most (1+2δ)²−1 and (1+2δ)⁴−1 times their respective spectral norms.
